title: Idempotent cleanup scratch notes for label reconciliation
content:
Context and goal:
- Quick personal scratchpad for an idempotent approach to dataset cleanup + reconciling labels across multiple passes.
- Problem: downstream heuristics and human passes produce inconsistent labels for the same logical items (e.g., PII, product names, instruction-answers). Need deterministic rules and a lightweight pipeline to re-run and fix without introducing churn.

High-level strategy (sketch):
1) Define canonical label schema (minimal set of conflicting buckets). Example: PERSON | ORG | LOCATION | PRODUCT | URL | OTHER_SENSITIVE | NON_SENSITIVE | INSTRUCTION | BOT_ACTION.
2) Implement deterministic precedence rules (higher precedence wins) instead of majority voting for certain types.
   - Precedence examples: PII (PERSON/URL) > PRODUCT > OTHER_SENSITIVE > NON_SENSITIVE.
   - Rationale: privacy-first — avoid under-marking PII.
3) Build idempotent transformer function T(record) -> canonical_labels that is pure (no RNG, stable normalization).
4) Use stratified sampling to test T against existing labels and a small human adjudication set.
5) Add small reconciliation pipeline that stores provenance and previous_label -> resolved_label diffs. Should be able to re-run multiple times without flip-flopping.

Normalization rules (for deterministic matching):
- Normalize whitespace, unicode NFC, lowercase except for language detection heuristics.
- Strip common noise tokens: [USER], <user>, <mask>, system notes like "Assistant:" at start of chunk.
- URL normalization: remove tracking params (?utm_*, fbclid), normalize http->https only for matching, but keep original stored as raw_text.
- Name normalization: collapse diacritics in matching step but keep original candidate as recorded. e.g., José -> jose for match.

Edge cases & heuristics (notes to self):
- "Acme" appears as ORG/product depending on context. Heuristic: if token adjacent to product-descriptor words ("model", "laptop", "pricing"), bias PRODUCT. If capitalized sentence-initial and no product words, bias ORG.
- Emails vs usernames: a@b.com -> URL label if it's contact info; if inside code snippet (backticks, monospace) label as CODE_SNIPPET and do not mark PII.
- Time-like things: "May 5" vs "may" ambiguous with verb. Only label as DATE if pattern matches and month name token present OR adjacent to year token.
- Bot system messages: label as BOT_ACTION when content contains system tokens or agent signatures ("Assistant:" "System:").

Reconciliation examples (toy):
- Raw: "Contact John at john.doe@acme.com to confirm."
  - Existing label: PERSON on "John"; OTHER on email.
  - Canonical rules: mark email as OTHER_SENSITIVE->URL_EMAIL (higher precedence). Keep "John" as PERSON if contiguous and capitalized.
  - Resolved: PERSON (John) + URL_EMAIL (john.doe@acme.com).

- Raw: "Try the Acme conda package"
  - Existing label: ORG:Acme.
  - Heuristic: context includes "package" -> PRODUCT.
  - Resolved: PRODUCT. (store provenance: was ORG, rule=adjacent_keyword)

Sampling for manual adjudication (design):
- Stratify by disagreement type: (label missing vs extra) / (PII vs non-PII) / (low confidence heuristics).
- Target sample size: start with 300 records: 100 high-priority PII disagreements, 100 ambiguous product/org, 100 misc (dates, urls).
- Adjudicators: rotate 3 people per batch to avoid annotator-specific biases.
- Adjudication form fields: raw_text, existing_label, candidate_label (from T), final_label, reason (short), notes. Capture timestamp and adjudicator id.

Idempotency checklist for transform T:
- No randomness anywhere (no shuffle-dependent tie-breaks).
- Sort candidate spans by (start_index, length desc) before applying precedence.
- Precedence table is a stable ordered list stored in config file (versioned).
- All normalizations reversible (store original and normalized).
- Log reasons for each change (e.g., "rule: url-normalize-strip-utm").

Implementation notes / quick pseudocode:
- token_spans = extract_spans(raw_text)  # deterministic extractor e.g., regex + dictionaries
- normalized = normalize(spans)
- scored_candidates = match_rules(normalized)  # returns list of (span, label, rule_id)
- sort by start, -len, precedence(label)
- apply_non_overlapping(scored_candidates) -> resolved_labels
- return resolved_labels + provenance_lines

Potential gotchas:
- Regex overreach: current url regex picks up fragments like "read more at example.com/section." Shouldn't capture trailing punctuation (".") -> add boundary rules.
- Language code switching: Spanish names with English context. Name-vs-word collision ("Pan" as name vs "pan" bread). Use POS and surrounding tokens to disambiguate.
- Code blocks: many false positives inside triple backticks. Skip labeling inside code fences.

Documentation / metadata captured per reconciliation run:
- config_version: semantic (e.g., v0.14) -> important for idempotency
- script_commit_hash: git sha
- sample_seed_for_adjudication: integer (only used for drawing sample for humans; T must not depend on it)
- run_id: timestamp-username

Quick TODO (prioritized):
- [ ] Finalize precedence table and add to confluence (small doc) -> note: link to playbook draft (CONFLUENCE-Labeling-Playbook-v0.9) needs update.
- [ ] Implement normalization helpers: email normalization, url strip params. (Diego owner)
- [ ] Add "skip-in-codeblock" pass to extractor (Samir owner).
- [ ] Create adjudication spreadsheet + small UI for rapid resolution (Priya owner).
- [ ] Run first sample (300) and collect adjudication in 1 week.

Open questions (for next sync):
- Do we want precedence hard-coded or allow per-project overrides? My leaning: default precedence global, allow project overrides with higher explicitness and require justification.
- How to handle historical label backfill that conflicts with business rules (billing tags, compliance flags)? Maybe add safety flag that prevents automatic rewrites of billing-related labels without manual review.

Notes to future-me: keep this file intentionally messy. Capture decisions here and then move polished rules to shared drive playbook. If anything changes in schema, bump config_version.

Snippets / quick regex ideas to stash:
- URL strip utm: s/(\?\|6)utm_[^&]+(&|$)//g  (double-check encoding)
- Email detection: [a-z0-9._%+-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+\.[a-z]{2,}\b (lowercase after normalization)
- Code fence detection: (?ms)^```.*?^```  -> skip region

Adjudicator micro-instructions (to include in the form):
- Prefer privacy, err on the side of marking potential PII.
- If a token could be PERSON or ORG and context is unclear, mark BOTH? NO — choose PERSON if first name-like word present, otherwise ORG. Add "both" only if explicit overlap (e.g., "Johnson Corporation").
- When marking PRODUCT vs ORG, look for adjacent product-descriptor nouns ("package", "model", "app").

End notes (links for follow-up):
- Quick test harness lives in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/label-scripts (PR 456 has sample stratum selectors)
- Jira ticket to track rollout: JIRA-DATA-4125

Random scratch ideas to explore later:
- Use a small deterministic decision tree to capture precedence rules instead of scoring; easier to reason about in review.
- Add a "stability score" metric per span indicating how many runs it changed in last N runs; use to prioritize human review.

Last saved by: Maya (quick mental note: make sure Diego, Priya and Samir get a short walkthrough next Tues)
